text:
mina: CI started failing for the onboarding unit suite after we switched the SDK to ESM-only for the edge runtime. Both vitest and jest show different failures but same root: mocks not attaching because module identity differs.

dev-bot: nightly-onboarding  build/onboarding #1302 failed
```
Error: Cannot use import statement outside a module
    at Object.compileFunction (node:vm:360:18)
    at Module._compile (internal/modules/cjs/loader:1092:27)
```

lucas: repro locally: pnpm -w test --filter=@redwood/sdk -- run unit. Vitest (vite resolver + esbuild) resolves the import path (dist/runtime.mjs). Jest with ts-jest (and transformIgnorePatterns) sometimes resolves to the cjs side (dist/runtime.cjs) or fails to transform the mjs, so our fetch mock ends up bound to a different module object.
sara: extra TS pain: ts-jest with isolatedModules and useESM flags changes transpilation pipeline and sometimes emits different helper names. Tests that assert on runtime internals break unpredictably. Also editors lose types unless package.json includes a types entry that matches the export path.
henry: quick fixes that made our CI green in infra: 1) add a tiny CJS test shim at tests/shim/runtime-require.cjs using createRequire to load the CJS runtime, so jest sees the same module identity; 2) for vitest, set deps.inline: ['@redwood/sdk'] so Vite doesn't tree-shake to the import entry; 3) ensure ts-jest has useESM: true + isolatedModules: false for test packages that import ESM runtime.

Example shim (tests/shim/runtime-require.cjs):
```js
const { createRequire } = require('module');
const req = createRequire(import.meta.url || __filename);
module.exports = req('../../dist/runtime.cjs');
```

jest.config.js snippets we used:
```js
module.exports = {
  extensionsToTreatAsEsm: ['.ts', '.mts'],
  transformIgnorePatterns: ['node_modules/(?!@redwood/sdk)'],
  moduleNameMapper: { '^@redwood/sdk$': '<rootDir>/tests/shim/runtime-require.cjs' }
}
```
vitest.config.ts snippet:
```ts
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    deps: { inline: ['@redwood/sdk'] },
    environment: 'node',
  }
})
```
mina: also added package.json tips: add "types": "dist/runtime.d.ts" and an exports.types mapping so TS will find definitions regardless of which export entry the resolver picks. That fixed a bunch of editor/ts-jest warnings.
lucas: longer-term options we discussed: (A) publish a tiny dev-only CJS package @redwood/runtime-test-cjs that re-exports the mock hooks (cleaner for consumers), (B) add a test-only conditional export in package.json that CI can opt into, e.g., an export key like 'test' resolved via NODE_OPTIONS or a small build flag. Both have tradeoffs.
sara: gotcha: on Windows the shim path hit long-path and backslash issues; solved by using forward slashes and keeping the shim near repo root. Also monorepo hoisting can create duplicate runtime copies if imports use different entry paths; standardize tests to import `@redwood/sdk/runtime` not `@redwood/sdk` to reduce duplication.
henry: I opened PR https://git.internal/redwood/sdk/pull/1043 with the shim, vitest inline config, jest mapping, and the types/exports update. CI green on linux/mac; windows flake rate dropped.

mina: actionable for devs who run into this: 1) try the shim + vitest deps.inline combo first; 2) if using ts-jest, set useESM and match extensionsToTreatAsEsm; 3) add types/exports.types to the SDK package so TypeScript consumers see typings. I'll add a short DEVEX doc with these recipes. Reopen if new stacks appear. :white_check_mark:
